claims.claim: Le Guin told Paul Morton that much of fantasy and science fiction is just the art of suggestion.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by Paul Morton, The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: fantasy and science fiction is just the art of suggestion

claims.claim: Le Guin told Paul Morton that a writer does not really tell people that much, but they think you have because they imagine it.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by Paul Morton, The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: You don't really tell people that much, but they think you have

claims.claim: Le Guin told Paul Morton that what she has learned as a writer is that you do as little as possible, part of which is leaving a lot of it up to the reader.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by Paul Morton, The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: leaving a lot of it up to the reader

claims.claim: Le Guin said her writing has tended to be shorter and more allusive than it used to be.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by Paul Morton, The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: my writing has tended to be shorter and more allusive

claims.claim: Le Guin told Paul Morton that she loves the sound of language and plays with word sounds in her head.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by Paul Morton, The Millions, 31 January 2013
claims.quote: I love language, I love the sound of language.

claims.claim: Le Guin told Jonathan White that the language of politicians is empty of everything but rather brutal signals and is something a writer has to get as far away from as possible.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, interviewed by Jonathan White, 'Coming Back From the Silence'
claims.quote: empty of everything but rather brutal signals
claims.page: section on language as a tool of forgetting

claims.claim: Bittner says the word 'tale' carries an archaic, distant tone that the word 'story' lacks.
claims.source: James W. Bittner, Approaches to the Fiction of Ursula K. Le Guin (UMI Research Press, 1984)
claims.quote: The very word tale has an archaic, distant tone

claims.claim: Bittner treats a guidebook title carrying many telling adjectives as a reason not to trust its user.
claims.source: James W. Bittner, Approaches to the Fiction of Ursula K. Le Guin (1984)
claims.quote: a guidebook with so many telling adjectives in its title

claims.claim: That essay credits Le Guin with a skillful use of cadence and sound patterns.
claims.source: An essay in Harold Bloom, ed., Ursula K. Le Guin: Modern Critical Views (1986)
claims.quote: a skillful use of cadence and sound patterns

claims.claim: Cadden puts it to Le Guin that Leese Webster is very spare.
claims.source: Mike Cadden, Ursula K. Le Guin Beyond Genre (Routledge, 2005)

claims.claim: Le Guin replies that Leese Webster is austere and that this fit the illustrator's talent.
claims.source: Ursula K. Le Guin, in interview with Mike Cadden, printed in Ursula K. Le Guin Beyond Genre (Routledge, 2005)
claims.quote: It’s austere, and that fit Jim’s talent

claims.claim: An essay in Olander and Greenberg's volume says Le Guin's straightforward stories deal in strong colors and plain fabrics.
claims.source: An essay in Joseph D. Olander and Martin Harry Greenberg, eds., Ursula K. Le Guin (Taplinger, 1979) — contributor not resolvable from the snippet window

claims.claim: Spivack says the style of A Wizard of Earthsea is suitable to its subject.
claims.source: Charlotte Spivack, Ursula K. Le Guin (Twayne, 1984)
claims.quote: The style of A Wizard of Earthsea is suitable

claims.claim: Spivack calls those monologues richly suggestive, leaving much unsaid.
claims.source: Charlotte Spivack, Ursula K. Le Guin (Twayne, 1984)

claims.claim: Dirda says the omniscient narrator confides in the reader like a friend.
claims.source: Michael Dirda, NEA Big Read teacher's guide to A Wizard of Earthsea (2008)
claims.quote: The omniscient narrator confides in the reader like a friend
